title: MIT Said the First Mars One Colonist Would Die in 68 Days

scenes.voiceover: Five MIT engineers ran Mars One's own plan through a simulation. The first colonist died in sixty eight days.
And not the way you'd expect. They didn't run out of oxygen. They drowned in it.
scenes.mainText: not too little oxygen — TOO MUCH
scenes.backgroundPrompt: indoor hydroponic plants under grow lights

scenes.voiceover: To grow food, the crew would farm crops inside the sealed habitat. Those plants flood the air with oxygen, until it becomes a fire hazard.
scenes.backgroundPrompt: rows of plants growing indoors under LED light

scenes.voiceover: With no way to remove the excess, the fix drains the nitrogen, the pressure collapses, and around day sixty eight, the crew suffocates. On schedule.
The founder's response? He called the study that predicted his crew suffocating a confirmation of his plan.
The full breakdown of why Mars One was impossible by design is on the channel. Subscribe to mindwired.
